quote: Section 9.2(a) covers *any* breach of or inaccuracy in *any* representation or warranty made by Seller. Read as written, this means the 10% cap ($1,840,000) and the $184,000 basket do not apply to **any** breach-of-representation claim—not just Fundamental Representations. ... Marrowind's indemnity exposure for the most common category of post-closing claim (inaccurate representations) is **uncapped and has no basket**. ... could expose Marrowind to a claim well in excess of the $1,840,000 escrow ... Amend § 9.4(c) to: ... (i) any claim under Section 9.2(a) based on a breach of a Fundamental Representation, or (ii) any claim arising from fraud.
reason: The memo flags the APA § 9.4(c) carve-out and explains that it removes the 10% cap for every Section 9.2(a) representation-breach claim, not only fundamental representations. It says this leaves Marrowind with uncapped exposure well beyond the $1,840,000 escrow. It also recommends narrowing the carve-out to fundamental representations and fraud. The memo does not suggest capping those claims at the Purchase Price, but the criterion does not require that.
